info.name: LLM request payload options: every request field with an example
info.description:
Companion collection for the llm-model-requestpayload-options tutorial: one request per vLLM /v1/chat/completions option, grouped into lessons, plus images, video and PDF.

**Setup:** pick an environment (top right) or edit the collection variables: `server` (vLLM root, for /health, /tokenize, /metrics), `api_base` (OpenAI-compatible base, normally {{server}}/v1), `model`, and `api_key`.

**Auth:** every request inherits a Bearer Token (collection → Authorization tab) with `{{api_key}}`. Leave it empty for a local vLLM without --api-key; set it for vLLM with --api-key, OpenAI, Google Vertex AI (gcloud auth print-access-token) or the Gemini API (API key). Folder 13 has requests that use only standard OpenAI fields, for hosted APIs.

 Test Results shows finish_reason, token counts and time; the Console shows the answer text. A 400 response means this model or server flag does not support that field, and the message says why. See README.md and lessons/.

variable.value: Explain what a GPU is in two sentences.

exec: if (j.usage) { const s = pm.response.responseTime / 1000; pm.test(`tokens in/out: ${j.usage.prompt_tokens}/${j.usage.completion_tokens}  (${(j.usage.completion_tokens / s).toFixed(1)} tok/s incl. prefill)`, () => true); }

item.name: 0. Server info
item.description: Check the server is up and which model name to use.

request.description: 200 = ready.
The `id` here is what goes in `model`.
vLLM version (fields differ between versions).

item.name: 1. Content: model + messages
item.description: What the model reads. Roles: system (rules), user, assistant (earlier replies), tool (tool results).

request.description: Only the two required fields.
System sets the rules; earlier assistant turns give the model conversation memory.

item.name: 2. Randomness (sampling)
item.description: How the next token is picked from the model's scores. For extraction/JSON use temperature 0 and nothing else.

request.description: Always the top token. Run twice: identical text.
Flatter distribution: more varied, sometimes odd. Run twice: different text.
Sample only from the smallest set of tokens covering 90% probability.
Sample only from the 40 highest-scoring tokens.
Drop tokens less than 5% as likely as the top one. (Rejected if the server uses speculative decoding.)
Same seed + same input = same sampled output, even at temperature 1.
Three independent answers in `choices[0..2]`.

Explores several candidates and keeps the best. Slow (~10x here) and rarely better for chat models; on Gemma-4 it leaked end-of-turn markers (<turn|>) into the text. length_penalty > 1 favours longer outputs.

item.name: 3. Length and stopping
item.description: Check `choices[0].finish_reason`: stop = natural end or stop string, length = hit max_tokens.

request.description: finish_reason becomes "length".
Newer OpenAI name for max_tokens.

Model may not end before 100 tokens. Watch what happens when the natural answer is short: it is forced past its end and produces junk (on Gemma-4: emoji repeated). Use only when the content really is long.
Stops at the first "4."; the stop text is removed.
Same as above, but "4." stays in the text.
Stop on exact token IDs. 107 = newline in Gemma-4 (from /tokenize), so this stops after the first line.
Ignores the end-of-turn token and always writes exactly max_tokens. Used for benchmarks; the text after the natural end is junk ("hi! hi! hi!").

item.name: 4. Repetition and banned words
item.description: Steer which tokens are allowed or discouraged.

request.description: Penalty grows each time a token repeats. Range -2..2.
Flat penalty once a token has appeared: pushes toward new topics.
Multiplier: 1.0 off, >1 less repetition.
These words are never generated.
Push a token ID up/down; -100 bans it. 9079 = " Paris" and 50429 = "Paris" in Gemma-4 (look IDs up with /tokenize). (Rejected if the server uses speculative decoding.)
Only these token IDs may be picked: 10784 = "Yes", 3771 = "No" in Gemma-4 (from /tokenize). With placeholder IDs the model is forced into nonsense.

item.name: 5. Output format (JSON, choice, regex, grammar)
item.description: Structured outputs: vLLM blocks every token that would break the format, so the shape is guaranteed (the facts are not).

request.description: Usually JSON; may add chatter or break. Compare with the next requests.
Guaranteed valid JSON, but any shape.

Guaranteed valid JSON with exactly these fields and types, yet look at the result: order_id -4471 and endless whitespace until max_tokens. The model wanted to write "#4471" ("#" is not allowed in an integer, so it picked "-"), and wanted to close the JSON before "email" (required, but not in the text), so it stalls on whitespace. The schema constrains the shape; it does not tell the model what you want.

Same schema, but the prompt names every field, says what goes in it, and says to use null when missing. Result: order_id 4471, email null, clean finish. Rule: describe the fields in the prompt AND enforce them with the schema.
Same as json_schema, vLLM's own field. Array of objects example.
Answer is exactly one of the options.
Answer must match the pattern.
Answer must follow an EBNF/Lark grammar: here a tiny SELECT statement.
Compact JSON with no extra spaces/newlines (fewer tokens).
Model continues your half-written assistant message. Forces the reply to start with {"name": ".

item.name: 6. Tools (function calling)
item.description: Needs server flags: --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser <parser for the model>. The model asks for a call; your code runs it and replies with a tool message.

request.description: Model decides whether to call get_weather. Look at choices[0].message.tool_calls. Server must run with --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser <parser for the model>, else 400.
Must call get_weather. Needs --tool-call-parser on the server (400 without it).
Round 2: give the model the tool output so it can answer in words.

item.name: 7. Thinking / reasoning models
item.description: Only for models with a reasoning mode (and --reasoning-parser on the server). Gemma-4 may ignore these.

request.description: On Gemma-4 setting reasoning_effort switches thinking ON (the default is off). Without --reasoning-parser on the server the thinking text lands in content (starts with "thought"); with it, it moves to message.reasoning_content.
Hide the reasoning text from the response (needs --reasoning-parser on the server to separate it).
Template switch (Qwen3 style) to turn thinking off.

item.name: 8. Streaming
item.description: Tokens arrive as server-sent events (data: {...}) instead of one JSON at the end.

request.description: Watch tokens arrive in the response pane.
Last event carries token counts.

item.name: 9. Probabilities and token IDs
item.description: Look inside the model's choices. logprob: -0.02 ~ 98%, -0.7 ~ 50%, -2.3 ~ 10%.

request.description: Confidence of every written token plus the 5 runners-up.
Scores every token you SENT: rank 1 = the model's own top choice. This is how the fidelity test judged outputs. First entry is null (nothing before it).
Logprob tokens shown as "token_id:1234" instead of text.
Adds prompt_token_ids and choices[].token_ids lists.
Prompt text repeated in front of the answer.

item.name: 10. Prompt and template control
item.description: How messages become the string the model reads.

request.description: No 'your turn, model' marker: the model may continue the user text instead of answering.
Show special tokens like <end_of_turn> in the text.
Add extra special tokens (e.g. <bos>) on top of the template. Usually leave false for chat.
Keep only 20 prompt tokens, cutting from the left (oldest).
Use your own Jinja template for this request. Refused (400) unless the server runs with --trust-request-chat-template, because a template is code that runs on the server.
Passed to templates that render documents; ignored if the template doesn't use them.

item.name: 11. Server, scheduling, tokenizer
item.description: Request bookkeeping plus the tokenizer endpoints.

request.description: Your own ID (shows in server logs) and a user label.
Lower = served first. Only with --scheduling-policy priority; otherwise rejected or ignored.
Prefix-cache reuse only between requests with the same salt (tenant isolation).
Free-form extra args for custom logits processors/plugins.
Shows how many tokens (and which IDs) a chat becomes after the template. Use it to find IDs for logit_bias / allowed_token_ids / stop_token_ids.
Tokenize a single word, no template.
Token IDs back to text.

Older text-in/text-out API: you write the exact string, including any chat markers. A chat-tuned model given a bare prompt without its template can produce junk (Gemma-4 here: "are are are..."). Use chat completions for instruct models.
Prometheus counters: requests running/waiting, prompt/generation tokens, TTFT histogram, prefix-cache hits.

item.name: 12. Images, video, PDF (latency vs quality)
item.description:
`content` becomes a list of parts: text + image_url / video_url. vLLM turns each image into vision tokens that sit in the prompt like text tokens, so **more vision tokens = slower prefill (TTFT) + more KV memory, but more detail**.

| lever | faster | better quality | how |
|---|---|---|---|
| image detail | `max_soft_tokens` 70 / 140 | 560 / 1120 (small text, tables, OCR) | `mm_processor_kwargs: {"max_soft_tokens": N}`; Gemma-4 accepts 70, 140, 280 (default), 560, 1120 |
| video frames | `num_frames` 4–8 | 16–32 (fast action, counting) | `media_io_kwargs: {"video": {"num_frames": N}}`; Gemma-4: 70 tokens/frame, max 32 frames |
| image transport | base64 (no download) | same | URL = server downloads it first (adds latency, needs internet from the pod) |
| PDF | text extraction (~1 token per 4 chars, exact characters) | page image at 560–1120 (keeps layout, tables, figures, scans) | vLLM has no PDF input: convert client-side (`pdftotext` / `pdftoppm`) |
| order | put media **before** the question | same | the question is read last, with the image already in context |
| reuse | send the same image again | same | vLLM caches processed images (and prefix-caches the prompt), so repeats are cheaper |

Compare TTFT/total time in Test Results and `usage.prompt_tokens` across the 70 / 280 / 1120 requests. Server limits that apply: `--max-model-len 4096` on the reference server (32 video frames ≈ 2.5k tokens fits; 2 pages at 1120 ≈ 2.3k fits). Multiple images in one prompt may need `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":4}'`.

request.description: Server downloads the image, encodes ~280 vision tokens.
Image travels inside the request: no download step, works without internet on the pod. A 1×1 red pixel here; replace with any `data:image/png;base64,...`.
~70 vision tokens: lowest TTFT; fine for 'what is this', poor for small text.
~1120 vision tokens: slower prefill, much better on small details and text. Compare prompt_tokens and time with the 70 request.
Combine vision with structured outputs: extraction from a photo.
Several images in one message. May need --limit-mm-per-prompt on the server.
8 frames x ~78 tokens ≈ 0.6k tokens: quick summary, may miss short events.
32 frames (Gemma-4 max) ≈ 2.5k tokens: catches more events; ~4x the prefill of 8 frames.

samples/invoice.pdf via `pdftotext -layout invoice.pdf -`. Cheapest (~450 tokens) and every character exact. Works because this PDF has a text layer and -layout keeps columns; scanned PDFs have no text layer, and multi-column papers come out jumbled.

item.name: PDF page as image, detail 70 (too low)

request.description: Page rendered with `pdftoppm -singlefile -scale-to 1100 -jpeg invoice.pdf invoice-page1` and sent as base64 (variable invoice_page1_jpg_b64). 70 tokens for a whole page: fast, but digits and small print get misread. Check the amounts against samples/invoice.txt.
Default detail. Usually enough for large printed text; compare amounts with 70 and 1120.

item.name: PDF page as image, detail 1120 (OCR quality)

request.description: Max detail: best for small print, tables, scans. Slowest prefill. Compare accuracy and time with 70 / 280.
Belt and braces: exact characters from the text layer, layout from the image (560). Most robust for important documents, highest token cost.

item.name: 13. Hosted APIs: OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Gemini API
item.description:
Requests that use only **standard OpenAI fields**, so they also work against hosted, OpenAI-compatible APIs. Choose one of the hosted environments and fill in `api_key` (and `model`).

| provider | api_base | api_key | model example |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | API key from platform.openai.com (`sk-...`) | a current OpenAI chat model |
| Google Vertex AI | `https://{{gcp_region}}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{{gcp_project}}/locations/{{gcp_region}}/endpoints/openapi` | output of `gcloud auth print-access-token` (expires after ~1 hour) | `google/<gemini model>` |
| Gemini API (AI Studio) | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` | API key from aistudio.google.com | `<gemini model>` |
| vLLM with --api-key | `{{server}}/v1` | the value passed to --api-key | your served model name |

vLLM-only fields from folders 2–12 (`top_k`, `min_p`, `structured_outputs`, `prompt_logprobs`, `mm_processor_kwargs`, …) and vLLM-only routes (`/tokenize`, `/metrics`) are **not** part of the OpenAI API: hosted providers reject or ignore them. Check the error message, and the provider's docs for the fields it supports.

request.description: GET {{api_base}}/models: which model ids this key can use (not every provider supports it).
The smallest portable request. 401 = wrong or expired key; 404 = wrong api_base or model.
Portable fields: system message, temperature, top_p, max_completion_tokens (the newer name for max_tokens; some newer models only accept this one), stop, seed.
response_format json_schema is the portable way to get structured output (no vLLM structured_outputs).
Image as a data URL: works the same across OpenAI-compatible vision models (no mm_processor_kwargs).
stream + stream_options.include_usage are standard OpenAI fields.
logprobs + top_logprobs are standard (prompt_logprobs is not). Some providers or models don't return logprobs.
Function calling is standard on hosted APIs (no server flags needed there).
